method: Read 775–850. Distinguish language comprehension, attributed institutional outcomes and independently verified legal facts. Definitions use official/public dictionaries; no current case-status investigation or audio reconstruction is claimed.
phrases: sex-based discrimination
unfair treatment or exclusion on the basis of sex
基于性别的歧视
The training explains how to recognize sex-based discrimination.
培训说明如何识别基于性别的歧视。
General language gloss consistent with the Education Department's description; not a complete legal test, current procedural rule or finding about this case.
sexual harassment
unwanted conduct of a sexual nature that harasses someone
性骚扰
The handbook explains how employees can report sexual harassment.
手册说明员工可以如何报告性骚扰。
General receptive definition, not a substitute for context-specific legal standards. The source's following essay remains unverified wording and is not silently replaced.
panel
a group selected to consider, discuss or decide a matter
评议小组；审议小组
A panel of reviewers discussed the applications.
一个评审小组讨论了这些申请。
Group-of-people sense, not a wall panel or screen control. The narrator uses it as local shorthand for the investigation group, not as a universal synonym for Title IX procedures.
subpoena power
authority to compel testimony or evidence through a subpoena under applicable rules
通过传票要求作证或提供证据的权限
The article discusses the committee's subpoena power.
文章讨论了该委员会的传票权限。
Different from voluntary requests. Source probably marks speculation about this panel's powers; the definition does not determine who actually has which authority in the case.
search warrant
a judicial order authorizing a specified search
搜查令
The fictional detective applied for a search warrant.
那位虚构的侦探申请了搜查令。
A warrant is judicial authorization, not simply a prosecutor deciding to search. The narrator's compressed search warrant power comparison is not a verified allocation of powers.
DA's office
the office of a district attorney, a local public prosecutor in the United States
美国地方检察官办公室
The fictional reporter requested a comment from the DA's office.
那位虚构的记者请求地方检察官办公室发表评论。
DA stands for district attorney; not a private defense lawyer or university administrator. This explains the role, not what the local office actually investigated or decided.
no matter what they find
regardless of the results of their inquiry
无论他们发现什么；不管调查结果如何
No matter what they find, we will review the evidence carefully.
无论他们发现什么，我们都会认真审查证据。
No matter + wh-clause expresses an outcome-independent point. In source they refers to the university investigation; its following authority claim remains attributed, not a general legal rule.
a big gap
a substantial interval or separation, here in time
很大的间隔；这里指较长的时间空档
There was a big gap between the two meetings.
两次会议之间隔了很长时间。
Completes there's such a big gap in 800. Gap refers to elapsed time in the narrative, not proof of what caused delay.
hearings
formal sessions where information or arguments are presented and considered
听证会；正式听取陈述和证据的会议
The committee scheduled two hearings on the proposal.
委员会安排了两次关于该提案的听证会。
Not simply the ability to hear sounds. Source refers to institutional proceedings; the card does not establish the exact rules, count or outcome of those hearings.
expelled
formally removed from membership or enrollment
被开除；被取消在校资格
In the novel, the student was expelled from the school.
小说中的那名学生被学校开除了。
Stronger than temporary suspension: removal rather than a defined pause with possible return. Source it appears qualifies the stated outcome; no independent case-status confirmation is implied.
egregious
extremely bad or seriously unacceptable
极其恶劣的；严重到不可接受的
The review found an egregious error in the calculations.
复查发现计算中有一个极其严重的错误。
Strong evaluative adjective. Not as egregious as compares perceived severity, not innocence; maybe/I guess/I could only assume make the narrator's proposed reason speculative.
brutalized
treated with extreme violence or cruelty
遭受残暴对待；遭到暴力摧残
The novel describes prisoners who were brutalized.
小说描写了遭受残暴对待的囚犯。
Strong harm verb in a personal account, not merely upset. Source was brutalized is passive and continues to physical and emotional effects; the example is fictional and non-graphic.
handling it
dealing with or managing the matter
处理这件事；应对此事
I don't agree with the way the team is handling it.
我不同意团队处理这件事的方式。
Handle a matter is manage/deal with it, not hold it in one's hands. Source the way and never seen before express the narrator's evaluation, not an objective uniqueness claim.
come up
appear or become available next, in this sign-off
接下来出现；此处指后续内容会推出
The next section will come up after the break.
休息后会接着进入下一部分。
Source points to the next episode half and an editing condition, not a promised publication date. Elsewhere come up can mean arise in discussion; do not invent a release timestamp.
segments: General discrimination and harassment vocabulary now has explicit support; receive assistance means obtain funding. Essay in the list remains suspect source wording. Official summaries clarify terminology but cannot authenticate that word or make the spoken overview complete legal guidance.
Put together means assemble people and panel now means a group considering a matter. This is an institutional group in the narrator's account, not a wall component or a criminal court by default.

The narrator sets a local shorthand: when she says panel, the listener should connect it to this investigation. It is not a claim that every Title IX investigation has the same structure or that panel means the law itself.

Themselves elliptically resumes Cornell is investigating from 785 and rhetorically suggests self-investigation. The reflexive refers to the institution in the conversation, not proof that all investigators are accused parties or that no external involvement exists.

Panel now has the assembled-review-group sense; little can minimize its significance and like is a conversational filler. The line describes the narrator's framing, not verified membership or competence.

All three role/authority terms now have explicit definitions. Probably marks the narrator's uncertainty and search warrant power conflates access to judicial authorization with powers of an office. The specific comparison remains unverified; do not approve it as a general legal account.

Read through 796: concession makes the following claimed limitation independent of findings. They resumes Cornell acting through its investigation, not every possible police or prosecutorial body. This explains the attributed sentence structure without certifying a sweeping rule.

They refers to the university investigation in 795; press charges is the everyday criminal-action phrase already taught. The lesson distinguishes institutional discipline from a prosecutor's role and reports the narrator's limitation claim, not a prohibition on reporting to authorities.

Take this criminally is nonstandard phrasing for handling the matter through criminal processes. In any way makes a sweeping assertion beyond the lexical gloss; retain the source and unresolved scope instead of endorsing it as law.

Read into 801 to complete there's such a big gap. I think/kind of limit the narrator's evaluation of elapsed time; the hesitation is preserved, and the joined sentence does not identify the reason for delay.

Completes the prior existential clause; such a big intensifies a time interval. This is a linked-fragment decision, not a claim that the noun phrase is a complete independent sentence or proof of unexplained misconduct.

Formal procedural sessions are now distinguished from ordinary hearing. At least gives a lower bound and like softens the numeric retelling; May 2025 comes from the preceding timeline, not new timing metadata.

Removal from enrollment now contrasts with suspension. It appears keeps the narrated outcome qualified; accused identifies status rather than a criminal conviction, and no current outcome is independently certified.

Temporary suspension and possible return now contrast clearly with expulsion; one of them narrows the three-semester timing to one person. The abrupt Who is expelled starts another turn, so retain the unsettled source boundary rather than merge sanctions.

The narration contrasts Matthew/Jonathan with Winston/Jillio and interleaves yes. Jillio varies from other printed names; do not authenticate a spelling or assign verified sanctions by silently reconstructing the exchange.

Involved in sexual activity is explicitly presented as other people's wording, not a finding of consensual behavior. Those other two refers to the second pair just discussed; the lesson preserves the assault allegations rather than normalizing them into mutually agreed activity.

Initiated means began and invited means asked someone to come. It could refer to the alleged assault sequence or its initial arrangements; the line does not uniquely specify its antecedent, and invitation never establishes consent to subsequent acts.

The vulgar phrase is already receptive-only vocabulary, but alum remains shorthand whose room reading was explicitly conjectural. Sender identification is the narrator's attribution, not authenticated message metadata.

Tied to is association in reports, not physical restraint; always is the narrator's generalization about repeated reporting. The new earlier card preserves attribution rather than treating repeated mention as independent corroboration.

Conduct refers generally to the alleged acts under discussion, not an inherently consensual activity. Jillia adds a name variant; keep the referent unresolved instead of silently merging it with Julia/Jillio/Giglio.

Not as ... as compares the narrator's supposed assessment of severity; sanctions are penalties. Maybe, I guess and I could only assume explicitly mark a guessed explanation for different outcomes, not a verified institutional rationale.
The abandoned So why are people so is followed by a question about expulsion. Vocabulary is supported but the missing continuation and change of question cannot be supplied as original speech.
Expelled/suspended/back form a broken correction with a dangling Winston. The next line explicitly says Winston's return is unclear; do not extract a definite individual's outcome from this fragment.

Could have come back is a past possibility for Winston, while but Jillio is back is an assertion about a differently named person. The false start and name variant remain; no identity or return date is authenticated.

Exactly zero is emphatic but charged academically sits uneasily with the preceding academic sanctions and subsequent DA discussion. Preserve it instead of substituting criminally or treating charges and sanctions as identical.

The office role now has explicit support. Zero of the seven is the narrator's count; investigated and charged name different stages, so a claim about investigation is not converted into a claim about conviction or independently confirmed case status.

Read into 832: that get attention is a relative clause modifying public statements. This can mean no attention-getting statements in that narrated period, not necessarily no statements whatsoever; the office role is now explicit.

Completes statements that get attention in 831. Get attention means attract notice, and at the time limits the period; it is not an assertion about today's publicity or a standalone complete sentence.

Read through 834 to complete the defendant list. Nobody knows is the narrator's broad publicity claim; until this year/two years later refer to the 2026 narrative after 2024. Civil filing, former sorority and fraternity roles are taught without asserting universal ignorance or verified current case facts.
Continues the entities and people sued in 833: a named bar and seven members. This is list completion, not a fresh accusation or a verified roster; the bar is preserved as printed.

Jane does states appears to introduce Jane Doe's quoted first-person account, but the printed wording is irregular. Preserve the source attribution issue and do not normalize the name/verb without confirmation.

Read into 837: physical injury is contrasted with perhaps more important emotional harm in the first-person account. Brutalized now has a precise non-graphic meaning; perhaps qualifies the relative importance, not a denial of the described harm.

Go through means discuss/examine the statements, not move through an office. DA's office is now a defined institution and second half previews later content; weirdest is the narrator's evaluation, not independently established fact.

Handling it means dealing with the case. Now in 2026 is recording-relative; something I have never seen before describes the narrator's personal experience rather than objective uniqueness or current verified office conduct.

That's refers to the second half previewed in 843–848; come up means become available next. Edit has the implicit episode/video object, and as soon as states a completion condition, not a calendar date. No release time is invented.
